title: Manage Stock Pools
readerIntent: Group balances for business purposes without creating another authority.
priorKnowledge: Understand warehouses, balances, scopes, and sourcing.
summary: StockPool is an Inventory-owned grouping used for availability and sourcing policies, not a separate module or duplicated balance.

sections.heading: Configure
items: Stable code, tenant/enterprise, purpose, active state, eligible balances/warehouses, product restrictions, service scopes, priority, safety policy, and fallback.
Use pools for sellable, reserved-purpose, campaign, channel, zone, segment, damaged/quarantine, or project-defined purposes.
Prevent cycles, duplicate balance ownership assumptions, cross-tenant references, and ambiguous priorities.

sections.heading: Purpose and ownership
paragraphs: A StockPool groups eligible balances or warehouses for a policy purpose. It does not own a second quantity; movements and balances remain Inventory-owned records.
Pools let projects express sellable, campaign, channel, zone, segment, quarantine, damaged, or other scopes without creating another module.

sections.heading: Membership choices
items: Explicit warehouses or balances.
Rules based on location, purpose, product, Store, channel, or segment.
Inclusion and exclusion precedence.
Active dates, priority, safety policy, and fallback.
Whether membership is evaluated dynamically or materialized and reconciled.

sections.heading: Example
paragraphs: A campaign pool contains stock eligible for an Electronics website promotion in three zones. A quarantine pool references damaged or inspection-pending balances and is never sellable.
The same physical warehouse can participate through different eligible balances without duplicating its authoritative stock.

sections.heading: Customize and extend safely
paragraphs: Pool types, priorities, and selection policy belong to Inventory properties and services where projects can extend them. A frontend cannot create arbitrary query rules that bypass backend validation.
Configuration prevents cycles, conflicting exclusive membership, ambiguous priority, and cross-tenant references.

sections.heading: Verification and operations
items: Explicit and rule-based membership.
Inclusion, exclusion, priority, and fallback.
Active dates and product or service restrictions.
Cross-tenant, cycle, duplicate, and ambiguous policy rejection.
Membership change invalidation and availability recalculation.
Pool size, evaluation latency, misses, and reconciliation.

sections.heading: Complete guide: How To Manage Stock Pools
paragraphs: A Stock Pool gives business operators a reusable group of Warehouses without creating another copy of Stock. For example, an enterprise can create a `UAE_FULFILLMENT` Pool containing Dubai and Abu Dhabi Warehouses.

sections.heading: Before You Begin
items: Create the Warehouses in the same enterprise.
Decide the Pool purpose and stable code.
Decide membership priority. Lower numbers are considered earlier by Stock Sourcing behavior.
Remember that a Pool does not make Stock available by itself.

sections.heading: Create And Activate A Pool
paragraphs: The same Warehouse may participate in several Pools, but it cannot be added twice to one Pool. A membership never moves or reserves quantity.
items: Create the Pool in `DRAFT` with its code, name, type, and optional effective dates.
Add each Warehouse as a `DRAFT` membership.
Set membership priority and review the ordering.
Make sure the Pool and Warehouses are `ACTIVE`.
Activate each membership.

sections.heading: Suspend Or Retire
paragraphs: Suspend a Pool or membership for a temporary stop. To retire a Pool, retire all of its memberships first. Never delete Pool or membership database records; retirement preserves operational history.

sections.heading: What Comes Later
paragraphs: Sourcing rules will decide when an application, country, delivery zone, channel, Store, customer segment, or item may use a Pool. Availability will then calculate eligible Stock from the member Warehouses. Neither behavior is part of the current Pool foundation.
For configuration, extension, security, recovery, and test details, read the [Stock Pool foundation contract](/docs/reference/commerce).
